text:
eva: FYI customer (acme-inc) hit an embeddings mismatch. They call /v1/embeddings with model=ritual-1024 and are getting 1536-sized vectors back. They say it started after a deployment yesterday and affects about 5% of requests. Repro steps included.

sam: ugh. first things: can we get the exact request headers + model field + full response header? suspects: cached prefix returning older-model embeddings, or a mixup in batch routing. :thinking_face:

eva: pasted their minimal repro curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"ritual-1024","input":["hello world"],"prefix":"acme:proj42:v2"}'
```
Response: 200, body contains "vector": [ ... ] length = 1536.

ingrid: do we have evidence of prefix reuse across model variants? our cache key should include model+quant+dim but maybe rollout changed dim without bumping prefix. :eyes:

leo: looking at the cache shard logs for tenant acme:proj42. found this entry sequence: 
```
[2025-05-18T14:12:01Z] GET cache key=acme:proj42:v2|model=ritual-1536|dim=1536 -> HIT
[2025-05-18T14:12:02Z] SERVE response vector.len=1536
```
then later we see requests that declared `model=ritual-1024` but the cache GET used `model=ritual-1536`. Key construction bug?

sam: interesting. do we tag cache entries by model string or by canonical model id? if our model registry was updated (ritual-1024 -> ritual v2 but backend image still returns 1536) that could explain. also batching can expose this if a stale KV cache entry (stored for a different dim) is used for a new request because prefix doesn't include dim.

eva: customer said they never changed prefix. they rely on prefix for deterministic cache reuse across runs. they used `prefix=acme:proj42:v2`.

ingrid: quick check: in serving runtime the cache key should be `${tenant}:${prefix}:${model}:${dim}:${quant}:${hash(input)}`. if `dim` is omitted due to an earlier migration, older entries could collide. can we grep code for `cache_key` formation?

leo: grepping now. found two places: one in prefetch path (caching by model.name only) and one in runtime (caching by model.id+dim). looks like a recent refactor removed `dim` from prefetch key. PR #8243 touched this.

sam: ok that explains inconsistent hits. mitigation steps: 1) invalidate affected prefix entries for acme:proj42:v2 (TTL purge). 2) ship hotfix to prefetch path to include dim. 3) add runtime assertion: if cached vector length != expected dim, reject cache hit and fallback to compute fresh embedding (and log).

eva: customer wants repro steps so they can confirm after we purge. can we provide a one-liner to reproduce locally?

leo: yes. run two calls back-to-back but force different model binaries: first insert a synthetic cache entry using admin-debug: 
```
# make fake cache entry (server-side, for debug only)
POST /internal/cache/set 
{ "key":"acme:proj42:v2|model=ritual-1536|dim=1536|hash=abc","value":[...1536 floats...]} 

# then call normal embeddings endpoint with model=ritual-1024 and the same prefix
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"ritual-1024","input":["hello"],"prefix":"acme:proj42:v2"}'
```
You should see a HIT and a 1536-length vector if vulnerable.

ingrid: added an ephemeral script for safety check (will push to infra:debug channel): it calls embeddings and validates len == expected_dim; if mismatch, it auto-records the request id, tenant, prefix and saves raw vector to /tmp for analysis.

cache-bot: Auto-detection rule `emb-dim-validate` fired 18 times in the last 2 hours for tenant acme:proj42. Suggested action: `invalidate-prefix acme:proj42:v2` or `enable-dim-check`.

sam: also billing: if customers got charged for wrong dims, we should offer to waive charges for affected requests and trace token usage. patch billing:flagging to finance. @finance FYI.

eva: I've told the customer we will purge their prefix and deploy a hotfix today, and to expect short degradation while we rewarm caches. asked if they want the temporary switch to a per-tenant prefix override.

leo: timeline: I can deploy prefetch patch to staging in 30m, rollout to canary 1 in 1hr if green. will also add the runtime assertion.

ingrid: postmortem notes for internal: root cause appears to be inconsistent cache key formation after refactor; contributing factor: prefixes are reused by customers as long-lived keys and expect stable semantics; mitigation long-term: key versioning (append cache-key-vN) + runtime validation + alerting on frequent dim mismatches.

eva: thanks team. I'll follow up with the customer after we purge and canary. attaching customer's request id: req_0a1b2c3d for trace. :thumbsup:
